researched_by: South West Water's community pages and South West Lakes Trust's own site pages, campsite booking pages and wild camping policy, plus the Charity Commission register, Wikipedia and local press coverage of the ANPR rollout
policy_summary:
The only water company found so far that both bans overnight parking outright and runs its own campsites - and it does both through a charity that is not the water company.

The rule first, because it is the most explicit statement of the overnight position anywhere in the landowner tier: 'Wild camping is not permitted at any of our lakes. Camping in car parks or on roadside verges is not allowed at any time', and 'The only legal places to park overnight are on our formal campsites.' It is put in property terms rather than safety terms - nobody has a right to stay because the land is privately owned - and it comes with a warning that entries on websites and apps advertising informal spots at these lakes are simply wrong and that wardens will move you on. If you have ever seen a Cornish reservoir pinned on park4night, that sentence is aimed at you.

The provision is the other half of the same policy and the parking pages do not mention it. Five lakeside campsites - Roadford, Wimbleball, Siblyback, Stithians and Tamar Lakes - between them about 114 pitches, taking motorhomes and in most cases caravans, from GBP19 a night off-season to GBP44 for a premium hardstanding in August, plus pods, belle tents and a cabin at Wimbleball. Hardstandings with electric exist at Roadford, Wimbleball, Siblyback and Tamar. Two of the five cap motorhomes at 20 feet and refuse towed caravans outright because of the approach roads. Season is roughly March to October, with Stithians and Tamar shorter.

Day parking is now private parking enforcement. GBP2 an hour, GBP3 for three hours, GBP6 all day at eleven lakes, with ANPR operated by Smart Parking at Argal, Roadford, Siblyback and Tamar - a ten minute grace period, a GBP100 charge if you miss it, and a mobile signal at some of these sites that will not load the app. All-day tickets explicitly 'do not carry over into next day'.
notes:
THE RELATIONSHIP, ESTABLISHED. South West Water Ltd owns the land and the water. South West Lakes Trust manages the recreation on it. The Trust is an independent registered charity, number 1079966, a company limited by guarantee, number 3969243, operating in Cornwall, Devon and Somerset and running around fifty inland water sites with roughly two million visitors a year. South West Water describes it in its own words as 'an independent charity who are stewards of our sites' who 'manage our sites for public access, conservation and recreation'. The Trust puts the ownership the other way round on its wild camping page, where the land is privately owned 'by South West Water Ltd and managed by South West Lakes Trust'. Both parties therefore describe the same split, in the same terms, from opposite ends: SWW owns, SWLT manages. It has run since about 2000 - South West Water backed the Trust's 25th anniversary in 2025.

What this means for the dataset. Every rule in this file is a landowner's condition of entry on South West Water land, administered by the Trust. It is not a byelaw and not a parking order, so it is enforced by wardens asking you to leave and, in the car parks, by a private parking company issuing charges under contract. The records stay under South West Water because that is who owns the land, with the Trust named throughout - if the management contract ever moves, the land does not.

The instrument governing the arrangement itself - lease, licence or management agreement, and its term - is not published by either body and could not be found. That is the one gap in an otherwise clean picture.

Trajectory: tightening on parking, stable on camping. ANPR was trialled at Argal from December 2022 and reached Roadford in May 2024 after nearly 25 years of pay and display, then Siblyback and Tamar. It generated real local anger - people wrongly issued charges, signs carrying the contract terms mounted eleven feet up, no signal to pay with - and the Trust's defence was that parking is about 6.5% of its income and pays for habitat work and footpaths. A charity funding conservation by contracting out enforcement to Smart Parking is an uncomfortable position and the local press has said so.

Height barriers are the quiet killer here. Colliford's three car parks are barriered at 2m, 2.1m and 2m. That is not an overnight rule, it is a physical exclusion of almost every campervan from the largest lake on Bodmin Moor in daylight as well as darkness.

Burrator sits on Dartmoor and is the exception worth watching. Free or donation parking, no barrier reported, three informal car parks and a great deal of grass verge, inside a national park with its own camping regime - and still subject to the Trust's no-overnight rule as a matter of the landowner's permission.
open_questions: The legal instrument between South West Water and South West Lakes Trust - lease, licence or management agreement, and for how long. Neither body publishes it. The Trust's filed accounts at the Charity Commission are the next place to look.

Roadford's pitch arithmetic does not add up on the Trust's own page: '36 touring pitches' but then 11 hardstandings with hook-up, 8 grass with electric and 25 grass, which is 44. One of the numbers is stale. Recorded as published.

Are any of these car parks gated and locked, or only signed? No opening or closing times were found for any South West Lakes Trust car park, at any lake, on any page - unusual, and the opposite of Severn Trent. If they are unbarriered all night then the only thing between a van and a night at Colliford or Burrator is a warden.

Burrator parking - free, donation box, or about to be charged? The Trust's page mentions donation boxes; a Dartmoor parking guide says the water company is 'not charging currently for this area of parking, yet'. That 'yet' is doing a lot of work.

Does the Trust run overnight vehicle stays anywhere, of any kind? Nothing found. If it ever does, it would most likely appear as a hardstanding offer at Roadford or Wimbleball rather than as a car park scheme.

Wimbleball's campsite pin and Exmoor National Park's Haddon Hill car park are 2km apart with different owners and different rules. Worth a human eye on the map to make sure the two records read as distinct.

sites.name: All South West Water lakes and car parks (managed by South West Lakes Trust)
sites.notes:
The estate-wide rule, and the bluntest wording found in the landowner tier: 'Wild camping is not permitted at any of our lakes. Camping in car parks or on roadside verges is not allowed at any time.' And, leaving nothing to interpretation: 'The only legal places to park overnight are on our formal campsites.'

Three things make this stronger than the equivalent statements elsewhere. It names car parks explicitly, so the usual argument that sleeping in a parked vehicle is not camping is closed off. It names roadside verges, which catches the lay-bys around Burrator and Colliford as well as the tarmac. And it pre-emptively contradicts the apps: if an informal spot at one of these lakes appears on a website or an app, 'the information is incorrect and you will be asked to leave by one of our wardens'.

The basis is property, not safety - the land is privately owned by South West Water Ltd and managed by the Trust, and nobody has a right to be on it overnight. Enforcement is by warden, backed at four lakes by ANPR under contract to Smart Parking. Covers roughly fifty inland water sites in Cornwall, Devon and Somerset.

sites.price_note: 2026: low season (Feb-Apr, late Apr-May, Oct) grass GBP24, grass with electric GBP32, hardstanding GBP32, premium hardstanding GBP36. Mid (Jun, Sep) GBP28/36/36/39. High (Apr, late May, Jul-Aug) GBP30/38/38/44. Includes 2 adults and 1 car; extra adult GBP7.50, child GBP3, dogs free, fire pit GBP14 a night.
sites.search_hint: Roadford Lake Campsite, Broadwoodwidger, Lifton, Devon
sites.notes:
The biggest of the Trust's five campsites and the best one for a large vehicle: 11 hardstandings with hook-up, plus premium hardstandings, on the caveat that 'grass pitches are suitable for tents or small campervans' and the hardstandings are what takes anything larger. Just off the A30 between Launceston and Okehampton, which makes it the practical overnight stop on that road.

The campsite is on the opposite side of the water from the visitor centre and cafe - about a 30 minute walk round the woodland path - and has its own postcode, PL16 0JL, not the PL16 0RL of the main car park. Sat-navs and websites confuse the two.

The published pitch counts do not reconcile: 36 touring pitches, then 11 + 8 + 25 = 44 in the breakdown. Recorded as published, flagged in open questions.

sites.search_hint: Wimbleball Lake campsite, Brompton Regis, Dulverton, Somerset
sites.notes:
On Exmoor, and the only one of the five that states plainly that all its pitch types take tents, motorhomes AND caravans - 5 hardstandings with electric, 7 grass with electric, 10 grass. Also the widest season, 2 March to 1 November, and the cheapest off-season pitch on the estate at GBP19.

Worth knowing that the activity centre and cafe run on a seasonal timetable that is much shorter than the campsite's - weekends only in May and September, seven days only in the school holidays - and the cafe was closed indefinitely at the time of research. The footpaths and the dark sky are there all year.

Exmoor National Park's Haddon Hill car park is about 2km away with an entirely different owner and an entirely different rule. Do not read them across.

sites.name: Siblyback Lake Campsite
sites.price_note: 2026: low (1-21 May, Jun, Sep) grass GBP23, grass with electric GBP30, hardstanding GBP24, hardstanding with electric GBP30. High (22-31 May, Jul-Aug) GBP30/38/31/38. Includes 2 adults and 1 car; extra adult GBP7.50, child GBP3, dogs and babies free.
sites.search_hint: Siblyback Lake campsite, near St Cleer, Liskeard, Cornwall
sites.notes:
On the edge of Bodmin Moor north of St Cleer. Small - 7 hardstandings, 4 of them with electric, and 8 grass pitches, 6 with electric.

The access is the constraint and the Trust states it: 'The access to Siblyback Lake and the campsite itself is unsuitable for towed caravans', and motorhomes are accepted only up to 20 feet. The approach lane is narrow with blind bends. A 7-metre coachbuilt is over the limit; a long-wheelbase van conversion is not.

The day car park at the same lake went to ANPR under Smart Parking in 2024 - pay within ten minutes or face GBP100, with the contract terms on signs mounted eleven feet up and patchy mobile signal on some networks. That car park is not an overnight option; the campsite next to it is.

sites.name: Stithians Lake Campsite
sites.price_note: 2026: low (20 Apr-21 May, Jun, 1 Sep-31 Oct) grass GBP24, grass with electric GBP32. High (3-19 Apr, 22-31 May, Jul-Aug) GBP30/38. Bell tents GBP70. Extra adult GBP7.50, child GBP3, dogs free.
sites.search_hint: Stithians Lake campsite, Menherion, Redruth, Cornwall
sites.notes:
The largest pitch count of the five at 28, and the only one with NO hardstandings at all - every pitch is grass, 15 of them with electric. Motorhomes and caravans are accepted, but on grass in west Cornwall in April or October that is a real consideration for a heavy vehicle.

Between Redruth and Falmouth, so the most useful of the five for the south Cornish coast. The activity centre runs most of the year on a Thursday-to-Tuesday winter pattern, closed Wednesdays, and daily from late May to mid September.

sites.price_note: 2026: low grass GBP23, grass with electric GBP28, hardstanding with electric GBP28, pod GBP39. High grass GBP28, grass with electric GBP36, hardstanding with electric GBP39, pod GBP55. Extra adult GBP7.50, child GBP3, dogs and babies free. Season roughly April to September.
sites.search_hint: Tamar Lakes campsite, near Bude, Cornwall
sites.notes:
The smallest and the most easily missed - 13 pitches and one glamping pod, near Bude on the Cornwall/Devon border, inland from the north coast. One hardstanding, seven grass and five grass with hook-up. Tents, caravans and motorhomes accepted but motorhomes capped at 20 feet because of site access, the same restriction as Siblyback.

Included because it is exactly the provision the parking pages do not mention: nothing on the Tamar Lakes day-visit or car parking material points to it, and it is the only sanctioned overnight stop for a vehicle in this corner of the estate. The day car park at Tamar is one of the four now under ANPR.

sites.name: Burrator Reservoir car parks
sites.price_note: No charge at the time of research; donation boxes on site. A Dartmoor parking guide reports the water company is 'not charging currently for this area of parking, yet'.
facilities: public toilets at the main dam
sites.search_hint: Burrator Reservoir, Burrator Discovery Centre, Yelverton, Dartmoor
sites.notes:
THE ONE A VAN WILL ACTUALLY TRY. Free, on Dartmoor, ringed by a single-track road with three informal car parks - the Quarry, Norsworthy Bridge (15-20 cars) and the Arboretum - plus, as one Dartmoor guide puts it, 'countless more grassy verges that have been taken as a parking spot'. No barrier reported, no gate time found, no machine, no camera.

And it is covered by the Trust's rule, which names verges as well as car parks: camping in car parks or on roadside verges is not allowed at any time, and the only legal place to park overnight is a formal campsite. There is no campsite at Burrator. The nearest sanctioned overnight vehicle stop on this estate is Roadford, some 30km north.

Care with the layers: this is South West Water land inside Dartmoor National Park, so the Dartmoor camping regime and the water company's permission are separate questions with separate answers. South West Water's own restrictions bite here too - dogs are banned on the dam under its rules. South West Lakes Trust also manages 25 scheduled ancient monuments around the reservoir, which is why wardens are about.
sites.geocode_precision: postcode centroid for the Burrator Discovery Centre address published by the Trust, near the main dam

sites.name: Colliford Lake car parks
sites.price_note: GBP2.00 for one hour, GBP3.00 for three hours, GBP6.00 all day. Free to Friends members. All-day tickets do not carry over into the next day.
sites.notes:
The largest lake in Cornwall, on Bodmin Moor, and physically closed to most campervans before the overnight rule even arises: three car parks with height barriers at 2m, 2.1m and 2m. Anything with a pop-top, a roof box or a Luton is out in daylight as well as darkness.

For anything that does fit, the Trust's page states directly that wild camping 'is not permitted at any of the lakes' and points visitors to the campsite at Siblyback instead. Charged parking applies and all-day tickets expressly do not roll into the following day - so an overnight stay is not just prohibited, it is unpayable.

South West Water's own rules ban dogs on the dam. Walking the full circuit is not possible because of a nature reserve and private land, which is worth knowing before parking for a long day.

sites.name: Roadford Lake main car park
sites.price_note: GBP2.00 one hour, GBP3.00 three hours, GBP6.00 all day; free to Friends members. Ten minute grace period for drop-off. Charges apply at all times the car park is open, 365 days a year.
sites.search_hint: Roadford Lake visitor centre and main car park, Lifton, Devon
sites.notes:
The day car park at the visitor centre, on the opposite shore from the campsite and with a different postcode - PL16 0RL here, PL16 0JL for the campsite. Recorded separately because arriving at the wrong one after dark is the classic way to end up parked overnight where you should not be.

ANPR went in during May 2024, replacing pay and display machines that had run for almost 25 years, and the rollout went badly: members and Friends were issued charges in error, and the local press ran the story of private enforcement putting people off their own lakes. Smart Parking operates the cameras across the four ANPR sites - Argal, Roadford, Siblyback and Tamar - with a GBP100 charge for non-payment after a ten minute grace period. The Trust's answer was that parking is roughly 6.5% of its income and pays for habitat and footpath work.

No gate time is published. That is the gap: a car park with cameras, no barrier and no closing hour, next to a lake where overnight parking is expressly banned.
